title: the overhead line counts every finished-in line as a suite, 0.00s included, so 'across N suite(s)' overstates what ran
body:
## Finding

`print_run_overhead`'s "across N suite(s)" counts every `finished in <n>` line, `0.00s` included (`lib/runlog`, the awk's `n++`). cargo prints one such line per test binary and per doc-test pass, empty ones included, so the count reads as more suites than ran anything. The summed seconds are right; only the count misleads.

Found by laksa-dc on 2026-09-03 reviewing hv's `fullcycle` on Laksa: `across 4 suite(s)` for per-binary times of 0.00, 0.00, 11.04 and 0.00. Re-read at devbin a7713e5 by laksa-dc, and re-driven by dc at HEAD on 2026-09-21: a four-line log with those times and `DEVBIN_RUN_T0` 15 s back prints `overhead: 1.36x -- 15s of GATE wall against 11.04s of reported test time across 4 suite(s).`

## Why not just count the non-zero ones

A `0.00s` line is not proof of an empty binary. cargo rounds to two places, so a binary running a few fast tests also prints `finished in 0.00s`. Counting only the lines above zero would swap an overcount for an undercount, and neither says which it is.

## Proposed default

Keep the count and say what it contains: `across 4 suite(s), 3 of them reporting zero time`. That clause appears only when at least one line reads zero, so every other run prints exactly as today. The line reports what the runner printed and judges nothing. No override: this is a label that states a fact, not a policy a project chooses.

## Test

A unit arm in `tests/unit/` feeding `print_run_overhead` the four-line log, red first on today's wording; a second arm with no zero lines proves the line is unchanged.

## vc's review (2026-09-21)

The proposed default holds: keep the count and add `K of them reporting 0.00s` when K > 0, since cargo rounds. Build waits on hv's order.

## Resolution

Fixed at `815e5f3`, reviewed by vc. On vc's review the clause reads `, K of them reporting zero time`, not `0.00s`: ExUnit's zero is `0.0 seconds`, and a count taken across runners should not borrow one runner's spelling. The UNDEFINED branch carries the same clause. `tests/unit/runlog.bats` gains the meter's first two tests: red first on the old wording, and a control that the line is unchanged when no suite reads zero; each is killed under mutation. Ships in 0.1.3.
